title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE BALIDAN SHATABDI SAMAROH OF SWAMI SHRADDHANAND JI AT KURUKSHETRA
subtitle: SWAMI SHRADDHANAND JI’S LIFE JOURNEY AND SACRIFICE ARE A SOURCE OF INSPIRATION FOR ALL: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced Balidan Shatabdi Samaroh of Swami Shraddhanand Ji at Gurukul, Kurukshetra, Haryana today (November 1, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President paid her tribute to Swami Shraddhanand Ji on the 100th anniversary of his martyrdom. She said that his life journey from Munshiram to Mahatma Munshiram and eventually to Swami Shraddhanand is deeply inspiring.
The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji had dedicated his life to the service of the Vedas and the upliftment of society. His life journey and sacrifice are a source of inspiration for all of us.
The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji was a strong advocate of social unity. In an address delivered from the platform of the Jama Masjid in Delhi, he conveyed a message of mutual goodwill and national unity.
The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji believed that eradicating the stigma of untouchability and uplifting the Dalits were the most essential steps for the progress of India. In his view, the evil practice of untouchability was contrary to the core principles of the Vedic tradition.
The President said that Swami Shraddhanand Ji revived and strengthened the Gurukul system of education. This breathed new life into the stream of Indian education and culture. He made tireless efforts to revive the ancient Aryan system of education, a cause championed by Maharshi Dayanand Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj.
The President said that the Centenary Year of Swami Shraddhanand Ji’s martyrdom serves as an opportunity to draw lessons from his inspiring life, his educational and social philosophy, and his dedication and sacrifice for the nation.
The President said that as we are moving towards the goal of a Viksit Bharat by the year 2047, it is of utmost importance that our citizens take pride in India’s rich cultural heritage while embracing modern knowledge, science, technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship. She expressed confidence that, drawing inspiration from the
life of Swami Shraddhanand Ji, the youth of our country will contribute to building an educated, self-reliant, harmonious, and empowered India.

date:

content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced the ‘Hirak Jayanti’ celebration on the 60th year of the formation of the state of Haryana at Kurukshetra, Haryana today (November 1, 2026).
Addressing the gathering, the President congratulated the people of Haryana for making significant contributions to various facets of India’s journey of progress. She said that this land, which spread the eternal message of Bhagwan Krishna’s selfless action across the world, has also established numerous milestones of human achievement in the modern era. The people of Haryana have made meaningful contributions in diverse fields, ranging from the freedom struggle to social change, democracy, literature, and science.
The President was happy to note that over the last decade, Haryana has made significant progress across various dimensions of women's empowerment. She said that the national campaign ‘Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao’, which was launched from Panipat in January 2015, has proven to be a highly significant initiative toward women's empowerment. She was happy to note the increase in gender ratio at birth in 2025 as compared to 2014. She expressed confidence that through the concerted efforts of the Central and State governments, this ratio will reach a level of parity. She was also confident that the ongoing improvements in areas such as women’s health and girls’ education within the state will gain further momentum.
The President said that in the history of Indian sports, athletes from Haryana have achieved extraordinary success in prestigious international championships. She expressed her appreciation for the daughters of Haryana for making the nation proud with their remarkable achievements in sports.
The President said that Haryana is scaling new heights in its journey towards inclusive development. The President said that the land of Haryana has gifted the message of the Gita to the world. She wished that the message of Bhagwan Krishna would provide the strength and insight to every individual and institution which is cont
ributing to Haryana’s development.

title: Vice-President Inaugurates National Organ Transplant Games 2026; Calls Organ Donation a ‘Mahadaan’
subtitle:
Vice-President Highlights Transformative Power of Organ Donation, Felicitates World Transplant Games Medalists

Vice-President Calls for Greater Awareness of Organ Donation, Dispelling Myths and Misconceptions

570 Transplant Recipients and Donors Set World Record for Largest Tadasana Congregation at National Organ Transplant Games 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 2:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the National Organ Transplant Games 2026 at Talkatora Stadium, New Delhi.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the National Organ Transplant Games 2026 at Talkatora Stadium, New Delhi today. 

The Vice-President paid his deepest respects to deceased organ donors and their families, whose selfless decisions give others a second chance at life. 

He described the Games as a celebration of courage, determination, compassion and the precious gift of life. 

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare; Ms. Bansuri Swaraj, Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha; and other dignitaries were present during the occasion. 

@mpprataprao @BansuriSwaraj @MoHFW_INDIA
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 1, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President described the Games as a celebration of courage, determination, compassion and the precious gift of life. He congratulated the Renal Care Foundation, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and the National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organization (NOTTO), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, for this important initiative.
Highlighting India’s civilisational ethos of selfless service, the Vice-President recalled the sacrifice of Maharshi Dadhichi as a timeless symbol of giving for the greater good. He described organ donation as a ‘Mahadaan’, through which hope can endure even in the face of loss.
The Vice-President noted that the organ donation movement in India has received significant impetus from the consistent emphasis placed on the subject by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi through his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ addresses.
Describing the Games as much more than a sporting event, the Vice-President said they celebrate the resilience of transplant recipients and demonstrate the life-transforming power of modern medicine. He commended the participants for their courage, discipline and sporting spirit, noting that their achievements inspire hope among those awaiting transplantation.
The Vice-President paid his deepest respects to deceased organ donors and their families, whose selfless decisions give others a second chance at life. He also appreciated living donors for exemplifying the finest values of love and compassion. He emphasised that one deceased organ donor can save up to eight lives.
Calling for greater awareness about organ donation, the Vice-President stressed the need to dispel myths and misconceptions, encourage informed decisions and motivate people to share their wishes with their families. He said the National Organ Transplant Games provide an exceptional platform to advance this mission by bringing together transplant recipients, donors, healthcare professionals and their families.
During the programme, the Vice-President released the ‘Zindagi Dobara’ Calendar and felicitated medal winners of the World Transplant Games 2025, held in Dresden, Germany.
He also witnessed an attempt at a world record featuring 570 transplant recipients and donors performing Tadasana together. Following the successful attempt, the organisers were presented with a certificate by the World Book of Records, New Delhi, for the “Largest congregation of Transplant recipients and donors performing Tadasana”.
The Vice-President joined the gathering in taking the Organ Donation Pledge and witnessed exhibition matches in Kabaddi, Table Tennis and Badminton.
Concluding his address, the Vice-President called upon everyone to make organ donation a powerful expression of shared humanity and to work towards a society where more patients receive transplants and fewer lives are lost waiting for organs.
The programme was attended by Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare; Ms. Bansuri Swaraj, Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha; Dr. D. S. Rana, Chairman, Sir Ganga Ram Trust Society and Chief Patron, NOTG 2026; Dr. A. K. Bhalla, Organising Chairman, NOTG 2026; and Dr. Anil Kumar, Director, NOTTO, among other dignitaries.

title: PM to Inaugurate Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 on 2nd November
subtitle:
Theme of Summit - ‘Invest. Innovate. Inspire.’

Summit to Witness Participation from Over 130 Countries, 9 Country Partners and 40 Ministers

13 States and UTs to Showcase Renewable Energy Potential and Investment Opportunities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 on 2 November at around 4:30 PM at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The four-day Summit will be held from 2 to 5 November 2026. The theme of the Summit  is ‘Invest. Innovate. Inspire.’
Bharat RE 2026 will attract participants from over 130 countries, including more than 40 Ministers, along with policymakers, investors, financial institutions and industry leaders. It will serve as a global platform for clean energy investment, industry engagement and technology partnerships. Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom will participate as Country Partners.
Thirteen States and Union Territories - Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal - will showcase their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities.
The Summit will be held alongside the 9th Session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH). While Bharat RE will focus on investment, industry and technology partnerships across the clean energy sector, the ISA Assembly will advance international cooperation in solar energy, including finance and institutional capacity. The ICGH will focus on green hydrogen technologies, investment and scale-up. Together, these three platforms will strengthen international cooperation and accelerate clean energy deployment.
Building on the legacy of RE-INVEST, India's flagship renewable energy investment summit, Bharat RE 2026 will provide an expanded platform for global engagement across the clean energy sector. The Summit will also host plenary sessions, ministerial discussions, CEO roundtables and country and state sessions, alongside business-to-business, business-to-government and government-to-government engagements to promote investment, partnerships and project development.  The Expo will feature over 400 exhibitors showcasing advanced technologies, Indian manufacturing capabilities and clean energy solutions across solar and wind power, green hydrogen, energy storage and other emerging areas.

title: Digi Yatra Begins International Passenger Trials at Seven Airports
subtitle: Trials to collect passenger feedback for wider rollout in 2027
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 4:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Digi Yatra has commenced trials for international passengers at seven airports across India, marking a further step in the adoption of digital technology in the country’s aviation sector. The trials, scheduled to run from November to December 2026, will allow eligible Indian nationals holding e-passports to use the Digi Yatra at designated airport touchpoints while travelling on select international flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.
The trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. Eligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, Security Hold Areas (SHA) and boarding gates, wherever the required infrastructure is available. Feedback received during the trial period will inform the planning of a wider rollout in 2027.
To access the facility, eligible Indian nationals must create an e-passport-based Verifiable Credential (VC) through the Digi Yatra mobile application. The process involves scanning the Machine Readable Zone (MRZ) of the e-passport, reading the embedded chip using the Near Field Communication (NFC) feature of a compatible smartphone, capturing a selfie and verifying the details. The credential is stored in the passenger’s Digi Yatra wallet on the device and can be used at airport touchpoints enabled for the trials.
The facility is intended to complement, and not replace, existing travel processes. Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete all mandatory airline document checks, immigration procedures and other applicable travel formalities.
The Digi Yatra’s adoption continues to expand across India’s aviation network. The platform has over 26.5 million users and has enabled more than 110 million journeys across 39 domestic airports, serving domestic airlines. A further 25 domestic airports are planned to be covered by 2027.
The Ministry of Civil Aviation remains committed to leveraging technology to improve airport operations and facilitate seamless air travel, in line with the Government of India’s vision of Digital India and Ease of Flying.

title: Coal Imports Decline by 5.83% in August 2026, Reflecting Reduced Import Dependence
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 10:52AM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s total coal imports declined by 5.83% in August 2026, falling to 104.57 million tonnes (MT) from 111.05 MT in August 2025, a reduction of 6.48 MT. The decline reflects the continued efforts of the Ministry of Coal to enhance domestic coal production, improve availability and strengthen the supply chain, with a view to reducing the country’s dependence on imported coal.
Key Highlights
1. Coal Imports by the Power Sector Decline by 6.39%
Coal imports by power plants decreased by 6.39%, from 22.77 MT in August 2025 to 21.32 MT in August 2026. The decline is consistent with efforts to improve domestic coal availability and reduce dependence on imported coal for blending at domestic coal-based power plants.
2. Imports by Imported Coal-Based Power Plants Register a Marginal Increase
Coal imports by imported coal-based (ICB) power plants increased marginally by 0.98%, from 18.13 MT in August 2025 to 18.31 MT in August 2026. These plants are designed to operate primarily on imported coal.
3. Imports for Blending at Domestic Coal-Based Power Plants Decline by 35.23%
Coal imports for blending at domestic coal-based (DCB) power plants declined by 35.23%, from 4.64 MT in August 2025 to 3.00 MT in August 2026. This reduction indicates lower import requirements for blending and is consistent with efforts to improve the availability of domestic coal for power generation.
4. Share of Imports in Total Coal Consumption Declines
The share of imported coal in India’s total coal consumption decreased from 21.20% in August 2025 to 19.30% in August 2026, a decline of 1.90 percentage points. This reflects a reduction in the country’s reliance on imported coal during the month.
5. Coking Coal Imports Decline by 4.18%
Coking coal imports decreased by 4.18%, from 28.49 MT in August 2025 to 27.30 MT in August 2026. Coking coal is an important input for the steel industry, and domestic availability remains constrained by the quality and characteristics of indigenous reserves. Import requirements in this category are therefore influenced by the specific raw material needs of the steel sector.
Sustained Efforts to Strengthen Domestic Coal Supply
The Ministry continues to focus on increasing domestic coal production and offtake, strengthening First Mile Connectivity (FMC), improving coal evacuation infrastructure and closely monitoring coal stock levels at thermal power plants.
Coordinated efforts with the Ministry of Railways, Coal India Limited (CIL) and its subsidiaries are aimed at ensuring the timely and adequate supply of coal to power utilities. These measures are intended to improve the reliability of domestic coal supplies, reduce avoidable import dependence and support uninterrupted power generation across the country.
The decline in overall coal imports, particularly imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants, underscores the importance of strengthening domestic production, transportation and supply-chain infrastructure. At the same time, imports by imported coal-based power plants and the steel sector continue to reflect their specific fuel and raw material requirements.
Ministry of Coal remains committed to further enhancing domestic coal production, improving evacuation capacity, strengthening supply-chain efficiency and promoting appropriate coal quality management to reduce import dependence wherever feasible, while ensuring reliable coal availability for the country’s power and industrial sectors.

The activity received an enthusiastic response, with approximately 1,500 visitors appreciating and participating in the initiative. He invited citizens to connect with the National Zoological Park, learn about rich biodiversity and join in protecting wildlife and the natural world for future generations.

During the walk, participants recorded 46 bird species and observed more than 500 individual birds in the designated area. The observations contributed to field-level biodiversity documentation and provided participants with a practical opportunity to engage in citizen science. The expert shared insights into bird ecology, behaviour and conservation, highlighting the role of birds in maintaining ecological balance including through natural pest control and their value as indicators of ecosystem health.
Addressing the participants, Director (NZP) emphasised that nature walks strengthen field-identification skills, deepen understanding of ecological relationships and food webs, support biodiversity documentation and foster a lasting appreciation of wildlife conservation. Shri Shah said that the 100 years of the manifestation of Akhand Jyoti, the 100 years of the birth of Vandaniya Mataji, and the 100 years of the sadhana of Pujya Gurudev Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya — the confluence of these three sacred streams is taking place this year. He said that the number 100 is regarded as a symbol of completeness. This year is also, in a way, a year of completeness for Indian culture and the Indian spiritual journey.
Shri Amit Shah said that Pujya Mataji herself performed austerities and illuminated the path for others. The flame that was lit 100 years ago has today become a symbol of welfare for countless people across more than 100 countries and in over 15 crore families.
The Home Minister said that in the four-day conference held in Haridwar this January, the entire Gayatri Pariwar had united and identified itself with the resolve of this Jyoti. Today, in the next stage of the same journey, two important events are taking place. The first is the ‘Deep Mahayajna’, which symbolises sacrifice, cooperation and dedication. Every lamp that is lit is a resolve that we shall use our strength for society, spirituality and the nation.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that, based on his experience, he believes the Gayatri Mantra is the path to complete transformation. It is not merely a religious or spiritual ritual. By experiencing the positive energy inherent in the mantra and enabling the mind, body and soul to realise it, it becomes a great path for bringing out the ‘sattva’ (essence) within us to the fullest. Shri Shah said that the 24 letters of the Gayatri Mantra are directly connected with our 24 auspicious nodes. Taking the 24 letters of the Gayatri Mantra as the foundation and receiving the sanskar (values) of its pure pronunciation from one’s Guru, if we awaken the 24 auspicious powers, the inauspicious powers lying within us are subdued and the auspicious powers emerge. He said that these 24 auspicious powers are linked with 24 kinds of attributes, which include foresight, restraint, austerity, courage, discrimination, intellect, protection, production, service, vitality, love, valour, concentration and others. He said that in a person in whom these 24 auspicious qualities arise, the path to ‘moksha’ (liberation) automatically opens and God leads him in that direction.
Shri Amit Shah said that the profound service rendered by Panditji by taking the Gayatri Mantra to the masses is as deep as the contribution made by the many sages, seekers and epoch-makers of India to Indian culture, our spiritual consciousness and the ‘sattva’ of the world. He said that Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya is the doctor of our spirituality. According to him, the chanting of the Gayatri Mantra awakens 24 kinds of auspicious nodes. When one correctly pronounces it from the navel to the mouth, these 24 nodes are activated and the internal secretions released from them develop the 24 auspicious powers.
The Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that many young people have benefited from the Gayatri Mantra. Their positive thinking, courage and memory power have increased, their capacity for interpretation has become sharper, and their decision-making ability has also improved. He said that Gurudev took these teachings to 15 crore families, and 15 crore families across the world is no small number. By generating faith in the Gayatri Mantra and establishing the tradition of its pure pronunciation, he not only uplifted the lives of individuals but also gave Indian spirituality and spiritual power a new life for the next hundred years. He said that we must continue to reiterate the clarion call of the digvijaya (victory in all directions) of this divine culture that he sounded, spread it, and carry it forward to the younger generation.
Shri Amit Shah said that a movement is rising through the Gayatri Pariwar, and it is the sacred duty of all of us to take it forward. This duty is to gather the auspicious forces of the entire world and guide the world onto the path of righteousness. We must continue this work until the last moment of our lives.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today attended the Diamond Jubilee celebrations marking the establishment of Chandigarh Police and graced the President’s Colour Award Ceremony of Chandigarh Police as the Chief Guest. Several dignitaries, including the Governor of Punjab and Administrator of Chandigarh, Shri Gulab Chand Kataria, were present on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering on the occasion, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that the President’s Colour awarded to Chandigarh Police today is a recognition of the force’s six decades of service, dedication and sensitivity. He said that making the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty is a matter of pride for any martyr and also a matter of pride for the organisation to which the personnel belong. Shri Amit Shah said that from 1966 to the present day, Chandigarh Police has continuously worked tirelessly to protect this remarkable city, thereby writing a golden chapter in its history.
Shri Amit Shah said that 141 new vehicles are being inducted into the Chandigarh Police fleet today. This will significantly strengthen rapid response, intensive patrolling, mobility, technology and modern policing. He said that Chandigarh Police currently ranks second in the country in terms of response time and, with the addition of 141 new vehicles, it will rank first nationwide.
Union Home Minister said that the President’s Colour is awarded to a force in recognition of more than 15 years of service, taking into account the discipline and dedication of its personnel. He said that over the past 60 years, Chandigarh Police has successfully worked towards safeguarding the entire country, serving as a vital force in the heart of the northern region. Shri Amit Shah said that Chandigarh, situated at the foothills of the Shivalik range, is regarded as one of India's most well-planned cities. However, when the country witnessed an era of terrorism, Chandigarh too was not spared. During that period, Chandigarh Police demonstrated exceptional valour and courage and, through its spirit of bravery, service and good governance, worked to protect not only Chandigarh but the entire region from terrorism.
Shri Amit Shah said that on November 1, 1966, Chandigarh was made a Union Territory and designated as the joint capital of both states. Coordinating closely with the Haryana Police and Punjab Police, Chandigarh Police has effectively managed the tri-city region. He said that the police force, comprising more than 6,000 personnel, has set benchmarks across the country through the exemplary discharge of duties by its Crime Wing, Operations Cell, Security Wing, Traffic Police and PCR units. Shri Shah said, Chandigarh has transformed a justice system once notorious for “Tareekh Pe Tareekh”, achieving an 85% conviction rate and an average case disposal time of just 140 days.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that policing in our country has largely remained focused on tackling terrorism, drugs, cybercrime and maintaining law and order. However, facilitating ease of access to services for citizens is also an important responsibility of the police. He said that through its Beat Policing App and this model, Chandigarh Police has successfully implemented an excellent system on the ground, ensuring that citizens do not have to visit police stations for their needs. Shri Amit Shah said that Chandigarh has the highest number of vehicles per capita in the country, yet the city does not face the problem of traffic congestion.
Shri Amit Shah said that Chandigarh Police has a Quick Response Time (QRT) of 10 minutes, while the average time taken by the police to reach a location is 4 minutes. Chandigarh was the first to introduce the Beat Policing system after 2015. He said that the three new criminal laws were also introduced by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in Chandigarh, marking the country's transition away from the three punitive laws enacted by the British. Shri Shah said that now that we have resolved to build a drug-free India, Chandigarh will be the first city in the country to become drug-free. He said that following the implementation of the new criminal laws, Chandigarh Police has increased the conviction rate in NDPS cases, securing the conviction of 93 per cent of accused persons and sending them to jail. This campaign against drugs and gangsters is a major achievement of Chandigarh Police. He said that from August 4, 2024, till date, 8,206 FIRs have been registered in Chandigarh, of which Chandigarh Police has filed charge sheets online in 7,590 cases. The police have also ensured convictions in 85 per cent of cases by improving the conviction rate. Shri Amit Shah said that this serves as a model for all police forces across the country, demonstrating that effective implementation of the new criminal laws can ensure the conviction of 85 per cent of offenders. He said that police services had earned a negative reputation due to the old laws, under which people were often deprived of justice for generations. Today, with a conviction rate of 85 per cent, Chandigarh has achieved an average time of just 140 days for securing the conviction of accused persons.
Union Home Minister said that the Government of India has provided Chandigarh with 2152 Artificial Intelligence-enabled CCTV cameras. He said that Chandigarh Police has won a total of 145 medals at the All India Police Duty Meet, including 35 gold, 38 silver and 72 bronze medals. Financial assistance of ₹8,000 per month is being provided to 130 families of widowed police personnel. Educational and sports scholarships amounting to approximately ₹2.25 crore are also being provided. He further said that 154 new vehicles were inducted into the force in 2026, while the housing satisfaction rate stands at 48 per cent.

title: EPFO's 74-Year Journey Built on Trust, Service and Commitment to Workers: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
subtitle:

Dr. Mandaviya Launches EPFO Services through WhatsApp

Launch of Automatic Settlement of Eligible Inoperative EPF Accounts; benefits extended to one lakh accounts involving ₹5 crore

EPFO's 74th Foundation Day Celebration showcases a Journey of Transformation, Compassion and Citizen-Centric Governance
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) celebrated its 74th Foundation Day today at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, marking its journey from a statutory provident fund organisation to one of India's foremost social security institutions, with a renewed commitment to technology-enabled service delivery, compassion in governance and the welfare of millions of workers and pensioners.
The celebration was presided over by Dr. Mansukh Mandviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth & Sports Affairs and Chairman, Central Board of Trustees (EPF). Shri Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment and Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi, Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Members of the Central Board of Trustees, workers, employers and other stakeholders also graced the occasion.
Addressing the gathering,
Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports
, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya highlighted that over its 74-year journey, EPFO has emerged as a trusted institution for the workforce of the country. He noted that the trust reposed in the Organisation is reflected in the ₹32 lakh crore corpus accumulated through contributions from more than 8 crore members, made possible by the dedication, hard work and commitment of the EPFO workforce.
Emphasising that social security must be driven by human sensitivity, Dr. Mandaviya stressed that every concern and grievance of workers must be addressed with compassion and empathy, viewing each worker with the respect and dignity they deserve as nation-builders. Commending the relentless efforts behind technological transformations like CITES 2.01, he called upon every official to focus on the welfare of the worker at the last mile. He urged officials to take inspiration from the ‘Panch Pran’ articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. "Seva is our sanskaar," Dr. Mandaviya underlined, and encouraged all to contribute towards accomplishing the goal of Viksit Bharat.
The Union Minister urged officials to focus on worker-centric innovations across domains in the run-up to EPFO's 75th year, adapting, building resilience, and evolving processes in tandem with changing times. He also extended Diwali greetings and wished for the light of success and prosperity in the lives of all EPFO officials, members and beneficiaries.
The
Secretary
, Ministry of Labour & Employment, Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar stated that EPFO, in over seven decades of service to the nation, has laid the foundation of and strengthened India's social security framework, creating a model worth emulating for coming generations. He emphasised that social protection and labour reforms must reach not just the organised sector, but unorganised sector workers at the last mile, noting that EPFO sets an example of how to achieve this through institutionalised processes. Observing that the day provides an opportunity to reflect on how far we have come and how far we have to go, he stressed that reform is a continuous process and requires constant evolution in the current digital age in order to effectively solve the common man's problems. He called upon officials associated with these reforms to adapt their mindset and perspective in tandem, prioritizing accessibility and ease of living for beneficiaries as collective efforts continue toward attaining the goal of Viksit Bharat @2047.
In his address,
Central Provident Fund Commissioner
reflected on EPFO's 74-year journey, from the founding commitment of 1952 to its present role as a national social security institution serving approximately 8 crore contributory members and 85 lakh pensioners, while safeguarding a retirement corpus of nearly Rs. 32 lakh crore. He acknowledged the contribution of officers and employees across the country, whose efforts have sustained service delivery while the Organisation has undergone significant technological and administrative transformation. Highlighting the need to make EPFO more accessible, reliable and humane, he emphasised that institutional trust is built through every claim settled, every pension delivered and every family supported during difficult times. He reiterated that the ultimate measure of EPFO's success must be the confidence and security experienced by its members and pensioners.
The impact of EPFO's technological transformation through CITES 2.01 was also showcased. A significant improvement in claim settlement was highlighted, with the average settlement time declining to 2.57 days in October 2026. The improvement reflects the Organisation's continuing efforts to make access to provident fund savings faster and more convenient for members.
Major initiatives and their benefits for EPF subscribers and employers
1. EPFO Services through WhatsApp
EPF subscribers will be able to access their PF balance, latest five transactions and passbook information through EPFO's verified WhatsApp service, besides receiving personalised guidance and assistance in completing PMVBRY-related requirements. This will make routine services accessible through a familiar mobile platform and reduce the need to visit EPFO offices.
2. Launch of Automatic Settlement of Eligible Inoperative EPF Accounts
Subscribers having Aadhaar-verified inoperative EPF accounts with balances up to ₹1,000 will not be required to file individual claims. EPFO will initiate settlement automatically after prescribed identity and bank-account verification, facilitating transfer of eligible dues to rightful beneficiaries. Approximately one lakh accounts involving ₹5 crore are expected to benefit.
Publications released and excellence recognised
Seven publications were released on the occasion, reflecting EPFO's commitment to knowledge creation, institutional learning, legal awareness and compassionate governance:
1. EPFO State Profile 2026:
Presents EPFO’s geographical presence, state-wise coverage, membership, establishments, claims and pensioner statistics.
2. Compendium of Judgements 2026:
Compiles important judicial pronouncements on social security legislation to facilitate informed and consistent decision-making.
3. Kendra Nidhi – Hindi Magazine 2026–27:
Showcases the literary and creative contributions of EPFO officers and employees and promotes Hindi.
4. Beyond the Desk, Beyond the Ordinary:
Celebrates the diverse talents and accomplishments of EPFO personnel beyond their professional responsibilities.
5. Reimagining Governance: Discourse for Excellence (RGDE):
Documents insights from the dialogue series initiated by PDUNASS on ethical leadership, compassionate governance and institutional transformation.
6. Shasan Vidhi Mein Karuna (Compassion in Governance):
Presents 83 real-life case studies from 62 Regional Offices, showcasing empathy and innovative approaches in resolving members’ grievances.
7. The Indian Journal of Social Security – Volume 1, 2026:
Features research contributions by EPFO officers on contemporary issues in social security, labour markets, digital transformation and pension administration.
The
Bhavishya Nidhi Awards 2026
were presented to recognise outstanding contributions by Regional Offices, Zonal Offices, individual officers and employees. The awards covered excellence in regional and district-level performance, grievance management, pension services, death claim settlement and PRAYAAS, PMVBRY implementation, technological innovation, training, publicity, cleanliness, exempted establishments and sports. The awards recognised the dedication, innovation and commitment of the EPFO workforce in strengthening service delivery and institutional excellence.
The 74th Foundation Day reaffirmed a common vision emerging from the addresses of the leadership: that the transformation of EPFO must ultimately translate into greater security, dignity and confidence for every worker and pensioner. As the Organisation moves forward, its endeavour will be to combine technological advancement with human sensitivity, wider social security coverage with dependable service, and institutional efficiency with compassion in governance.
The journey of EPFO is not merely a story of institutional growth; it is a continuing commitment to ensure that the fruits of a worker's years of labour translate into security, dignity and peace of mind for the worker and the family.

content:
To disseminate Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Swadeshi in every home,’ ‘Vocal for Local,’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ among the masses, the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) organized the ‘Khadi Diwali Fest-2026’ at NDMC Palika Park, Connaught Place, New Delhi (opposite Regal Cinema). The event featured a special interaction with media representatives and a ‘Diwali Milan’ (Diwali get together). KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel joined the event as the chief guest. Held under the theme ‘Khadi-wali Diwali,’ the event aims to encourage citizens to adopt Khadi and Swadeshi products during Diwali and other festivals, provide greater recognition to the creations of Indian artisans and rural entrepreneurs, and, in particular, connect the youth with the Swadeshi movement.
Speaking on the occasion, KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel opined that the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, envisioned Khadi not merely as a fabric, but as a symbol of self-reliance, self-respect, and economic independence. Today, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Khadi and *Swadeshi* (indigenous) movement has gained new momentum and widespread public participation. The Prime Minister’s call for Har Ghar  Swadeshi, Ghar Ghar Swadehi’   extends beyond the mere purchase of indigenous goods; it s a comprehensive campaign aimed at fostering a sense of pride in Indian products, encouraging local producers, and strengthening the nation’s economic self-reliance.
Shri Goel reitrerated that the festive season is of immense significance to the Indian economy, local markets, and artisans. If every family prioritizes Khadi and other *Swadeshi* products during the festive season, the direct benefits reach millions of artisans, weavers, rural entrepreneurs, and their families across the country. He emphasized that purchasing *Swadeshi* products is not just a consumer choice, but a vital contribution by citizens toward strengthening the national economy and local employment.
The KVIC Chairman specifically urged the youth—including Gen-Z—to join the *Swadeshi* movement, highlighting that today’s youth are highly conscious of fashion, design, technology, and innovative ideas. By integrating Khadi and village industry products with modern designs, attractive presentation, superior branding, and contemporary lifestyles, these items can become even more popular among the youth. He added that young people can be more than just consumers of *Swadeshi* products; they can also serve as brand ambassadors, designers, digital promoters and entrepreneurs.
Shri Goel said that the role of the youth is crucial in realizing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of "Local to Global." Through social media, e-commerce, digital marketing, and startups, the youth can help take Khadi and village industry products to every nook and corner of the country, while also establishing a new identity for them in international markets. He further stated that to convey Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Viksit Bharat @ 2047’ and the ‘Vocal for Local’ initiative to the younger generation, KVIC has launched a podcast titled ‘Baat Khadi Ki’. Through this, efforts are being made to connect Gen-Z with Khadi and the *Swadeshi* (indigenous) movement by exploring topics such as the legacy of Khadi, modern fashion, innovation, and youth entrepreneurship. This initiative will help popularize Khadi among the new generation and strengthen the resolve for an *Atmanirbhar Bharat* (Self-reliant India).
Interacting with media representatives, Shri Goel noted that the Khadi and Village Industries sector has witnessed unprecedented progress, driven by the visionary thinking and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. In the financial year 2025-26, the turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector exceeded Rs 1.87 lakh crore, while the sector has provided employment to over 2.04 crore people. He expressed confidence that, in the near future, the sector will achieve a turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore.
The ‘Khadi Diwali Fest-2026,’ which commenced on October 31, offers a special discount of 20 percent on Khadi products and 10 percent on Village Industry products. This festival reinforces the message that this Diwali, we should not only light *diyas* (lamps) in our homes but also spread the light of joy in the lives of millions of artisans and rural families across the country by embracing Khadi and Swadeshi products.

title: Shri Dinesh V. Ganvir Takes Charge as Director General of GSI; Reaffirms Focus on Mineral Security, Scientific Excellence and Technological Advancement
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 3:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Dinesh Vitthalrao Ganvir has assumed the charge as the 55th Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI), an attached office of the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. With more than three decades of experience spanning geological investigations, mineral exploration, engineering geology and institutional leadership, Shri Dinesh V. Ganvir brings to the office extensive scientific, technical and administrative experience.
Shri Dinesh V. Ganvir joined the Geological Survey of India on 1st July 1994, following the completion of his Master's degree in Geology from RTMNU University, Nagpur. Over a career spanning more than 32 years, he has served in a range of scientific, technical and administrative positions across GSI's Central Region, North-Eastern Region and Northern Region. Immediately prior to assuming the charge of Director General, he was serving as Additional Director General and Head of Department, Central Region, Nagpur, while also holding the additional charge of National Mission Head-II.
His contributions span geological mapping, mineral exploration, engineering geology and multidisciplinary geoscientific studies. His assignments include thematic mapping in the Western Bastar Craton; gold and diamond exploration in the Sakoli Fold Belt of Maharashtra; and geoscientific studies associated with the conservation of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Bhimbetka Rock Shelters and Ellora Caves. He has represented GSI at several international forums, including the India–Peru Joint Working Group, the Russia–India Mining Sub-Group and IMARC 2022 in Australia.
In leadership assignments, particularly as  National Mission Head-II, Shri Dinesh V. Ganvir was associated with the planning and monitoring of multidisciplinary field programmes and nationwide mineral exploration, including spearheading a five fold jump in investigations for critical and strategic minerals in recent time and preparation of geological reports and exploration blocks for mineral auctions process in line with GSI's national mandate. During this tenure, he made significant contributions to the nation’s mineral exploration and resource development initiatives, facilitating the handover of 359 Geological Reports and 377 Geological Memorandums. Of these, 202 blocks pertained to critical minerals, of which 40 have been successfully auctioned, while 56 blocks under the Exploration Licence (EL) regime were handed over, of which 11 have been auctioned, under Tranche I & II.
On assuming charge of Director General, Shri Dinesh V. Ganvir underscored the importance of enhancing the scientific depth, relevance and national impact of GSI's work. A key priority will be to intensify exploration for critical and strategic minerals through integrated geoscientific investigations, advanced mineral prospectivity mapping and systematic generation of scientifically robust, auction-ready mineral blocks. These efforts will support the country's objectives of strengthening mineral security, reducing import dependence and advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat.
He also emphasised the need to harness emerging technologies and advanced data analytics in conjunction with rigorous field-based investigations. The integration of modern geoscientific tools and methods is expected to improve the precision and efficiency of exploration. Strengthening laboratory infrastructure, upgrading analytical capabilities and offshore exploration will also be important areas of focus.
Beyond mineral exploration, GSI will continue to strengthen its contributions to fundamental geoscientific research, landslide early warning, glacial and cryospheric studies, major infrastructure projects and hazard assessment. These areas of work are vital to informed policymaking, infrastructure planning, disaster preparedness and sustainable development. The emphasis will be on generating reliable, science-based inputs that address the country's evolving developmental and societal priorities.
Emphasising institutional development, Shri Dinesh V. Ganvir highlighted the need to empower scientific personnel, foster innovation, recognise merit and performance, and strengthen coordination among National Missions, Regional offices and State Units. Efficient resource utilisation and timely delivery of high-quality scientific outputs will remain central to enhancing GSI's effectiveness.
Under his leadership, GSI will seek to build on its rich scientific legacy while responding to the demands of a rapidly evolving geoscientific and technological landscape. With a renewed focus on scientific excellence, innovation, collaboration and outcome-oriented work, the organisation will continue to play a pivotal role in strengthening India's mineral resource base, supporting infrastructure development, enhancing disaster resilience and contributing to the national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju represented Government of India at
the ceremony for raising and consecration of 108 Stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, led by His Majesty The King of Bhutan on 01 November 2026. The 108 Stupas project was conceived by His Majesty The King of Bhutan who also steered its implementation. In a single day, thousands of volunteers erected 108 Stupas, each 15 metres tall and separated by 108 metres on an 11.7 kilometre stretch along the Aie (Mau) River within Gelephu Mindfulness City near the border with Assam. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi

Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck
and met with the Prime Minister of Bhutan,
Dasho Tshering Tobgay
. title: Union Minister for Railways Flags Off Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express Train
subtitle:
Union Ministers Pralhad Joshi, H. D. Kumaraswamy, Minister of State for Railways V. Somanna and Other Dignitaries Also Join Flag-off Ceremony

New Vande Bharat Sleeper Express to Enhance Connectivity Between Bengaluru and Mumbai, Connecting India's IT and Startup Capital with Its Financial Capital: Sh. Ashwini Vaishnaw

Modern Overnight Rail Connectivity to Benefit Professionals, Entrepreneurs, Students, Traders and Tourists
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today flagged off the SMVT Bengaluru-Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express in the presence of Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister Shri H. D. Kumaraswamy, Minister of State for Railways Shri V. Somanna, Minister of State Sushri Shobha Karandlaje and other dignitaries. The flag-off ceremony marks an important step towards strengthening modern overnight rail connectivity between two of India's leading metropolitan and economic centres.
Hon’ble Minister of Railways Shri @AshwiniVaishnaw, along with other dignitaries, flagged off the Bengaluru–Mumbai #VandeBharat_Sleeper train. https://t.co/2Gro8cQO5B
— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia)
November 1, 2026
The introduction of this next-generation sleeper train will provide passengers with an additional modern, comfortable and efficient travel option between Bengaluru and Mumbai. The service is expected to benefit professionals, entrepreneurs, business travellers, students, traders and tourists while strengthening connectivity across important regional centres in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.
Following the introduction of Vande Bharat Sleeper services on the Howrah-Guwahati corridor in January 2026, and the flagging off of the Varanasi-New Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper train yesterday, the Bengaluru-Mumbai service further expands the network of modern overnight rail travel and reinforces Indian Railways' commitment to passenger-centric mobility.
Highlighting the introduction of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express, Shri Vaishnaw said that the service would connect Bengaluru, the country's IT and startup capital, with Mumbai, its financial capital. The train will run via Anantapur and Guntakal in Andhra Pradesh; Raichur, Yadgir and Kalaburagi in Karnataka; and Solapur, Pune and Kalyan in Maharashtra, providing improved overnight connectivity to several parts of North Karnataka that previously lacked access to premium, world-class train services. He also announced that the next Vande Bharat Sleeper service for Karnataka would originate from Bengaluru, connect the northern parts of the state towards the Hubballi region and proceed towards Pune and Mumbai.
The Union Minister further announced that Vande Bharat services between Bengaluru and Mangaluru are expected to commence within the next few weeks, following the completion of electrification and successful testing on the route. The service will strengthen connectivity between Bengaluru and coastal Karnataka. He emphasised that the new service would provide faster, more comfortable and world-class rail connectivity to the region. He also highlighted the importance of modern railway infrastructure, technology-driven improvements and the expansion of high-speed services in strengthening passenger connectivity and supporting the economic development of Karnataka.
The Union Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw highlighted the expansion of high-speed rail connectivity in Karnataka and the development of new railway corridors to strengthen regional connectivity and promote economic integration. Highlighting the expected reduction in travel time, he stated that the Bengaluru-Chennai journey would take just 73 minutes, while Bengaluru-Hyderabad connectivity would be covered in approximately 2 hours and 10 minutes.
Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Railways in strengthening railway connectivity across Karnataka, particularly in North Karnataka. He highlighted the increased allocation of funds for railway infrastructure development and appreciated the significant progress made in railway development works in Karnataka. Shri Joshi emphasized that this robust investment has driven both infrastructure expansion and safety enhancements, pointing out that accident rates have plummeted from 135 to 16 following the rollout of the Kavach protection system, with a clear institutional target of achieving zero accidents. He also welcomed the introduction of new Vande Bharat services and the announcement of additional high-speed rail corridors, stating that these initiatives would improve passenger connectivity, enhance regional development and provide better access to modern rail services across Karnataka.
Union Minister Shri H. D. Kumaraswamy welcomed the introduction of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper service, the proposed Vande Bharat connectivity between Bengaluru and Mangaluru, and the planned rail connectivity linking Bengaluru with Pune. He noted that these initiatives would benefit not only the people of Karnataka but also the large number of migrant workers and families from states such as West Bengal, Assam and Bihar residing in Bengaluru, while improving passenger convenience and regional connectivity.
Union Minister of State for Railways Shri V. Somanna mentioned the significant transformation of railway infrastructure in Karnataka, with emphasis on expediting long-pending projects, strengthening rail connectivity and improving passenger amenities across the state. He highlighted that railway infrastructure development works worth approximately ₹52,000 crore are underway in the State. He appreciated the efforts of the Railway Minister in restoring train services, accelerating the construction of railway overbridges and underbridges, and modernising railway stations across Bengaluru, district headquarters and other important centres.
Connecting Two Major Economic and Commercial Centres
The new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express will establish an important overnight rail link between Bengaluru, a leading hub for information technology, innovation, education and entrepreneurship, and Mumbai, the country's financial and commercial capital.
Both metropolitan centres witness substantial movement of professionals, entrepreneurs, students, business travellers and families. The new service will offer passengers an additional convenient travel option, enabling them to undertake long-distance journeys overnight and reach their destination the following day.
The train will connect important stations along its route, including Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Yadgir, Wadi, Kalaburagi, Solapur, Pune and Kalyan. This will strengthen connectivity across parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra, providing improved access to important commercial, educational and regional centres.
The train will depart SMVT Bengaluru at 19:45 hours and arrive at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai, at 11:55 hours the following day. In the return direction, it will depart CSMT at 20:10 hours and reach SMVT Bengaluru at 12:00 hours the next day. The service will operate six days a week, except Monday in the Bengaluru-originating direction and Tuesday in the Mumbai-originating direction.
The overnight schedule will allow passengers to make more effective use of their daytime while travelling comfortably between the two metropolitan centres. Passengers from cities and towns along the route will also benefit from an additional modern rail travel option.
The flag-off of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express marks another important milestone in Indian Railways' ongoing efforts to transform passenger transportation through modern infrastructure, advanced technology and improved connectivity. Indian Railways remains committed to developing a modern, efficient, safe and passenger-centric transportation network that supports India's economic growth and connects metropolitan centres with emerging regional hubs.

title: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Performs Bhoomipujan of Multi-Modal Logistics Park at Sindi Railway
subtitle: - Project to boost exports, reduce transportation costs and create employment opportunities for local residents
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 6:09PM by PIB Mumbai
content:
Wardha,
November 1, 2026:
Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari said that the Multi-Modal Logistics Park being developed at Sindi Railway would boost direct exports to international markets through Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and create employment opportunities for local residents.
The project is being developed by National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML), a special purpose vehicle of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), through AMARA TRANZ Solution. The bhoomipujan ceremony of the project was held at Sindi Railway today in the presence of Guardian Minister Dr. Pankaj Bhoyar, MLA Sameer Kunawar, District Collector Vanmathi C, former MP Ramdas Tadas and Sindi Railway Municipal Council President Rani Kalode, among others.
Gadkari said the Multi-Modal Logistics Park would facilitate the direct export of cotton, cotton lint, yarn, oranges and vegetables from Vidarbha to international markets through Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority. The project would also reduce transportation time for cargo moving from Vidarbha through the Mumbai–Colombo–Dhaka route. He added that the first rake carrying Maruti cars had already commenced operations from the project.
The project is being jointly developed by National Highways Logistics Management Limited and Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority across 150 acres of land near Sindi Railway railway station. Through the dry port at Sindi Railway, cotton, cotton lint, textiles and oranges from Vidarbha will be transported directly to Bangladesh via Haldia in Kolkata, without having to travel to Mumbai. This is expected to reduce transportation costs per container from ₹1.5 lakh to ₹1 lakh, benefiting farmers in the Vidarbha region.
The Multi-Modal Logistics Park, being developed with funding provisions from the Central and State Governments on the Nagpur–Wardha district border, will be connected to the dry port at Sindi Railway. Facilities such as cold storage and warehouses will be established at the site, enabling the consolidation of major industries from Nagpur and Wardha. Exporter clusters will also be developed at the location.
With a customs office to be established at Sindi Railway, the facility will handle containers from across the country and abroad, further strengthening the region's logistics and export infrastructure.

title: Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment Issues Factual Report With Regard To The Claim—Appearing In A Report Published In The Central Chronicle (Bhopal) On October 31, 2026
subtitle: Claim That MAPCET Made Payments Amounting To Crores Based On Placements Without Verifying The Placement Data, Is Entirely Incorrect And Baseless
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 3:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment has issued a factual report with regard to the claim—appearing in a report published in
The Central Chronicle (Bhopal),
on October 31, 2026.
The claim with regard to Madhya Pradesh Council for Employment and Training (MAPCET), having made payments amounting to crores based on placements without verifying the placement data,
is entirely incorrect and baseless.
The factual report is attached herewith, for publishing the same with accuracy and factual context:
FACTUAL REPORT REGARDING THE NEWS ITEM PUBLISHED IN
CENTRAL CHRONICLE, BHOPAL, ON 31 OCTOBER 2026
The Office of the Commissioner, Scheduled Caste Development Department, sanctioned an amount of Rs. 3,241.37 lakh for skill development training under the “Special Central Assistance for Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan” head. Against this amount, a total of Rs. 2,945.37 lakh was made available to the Madhya Pradesh Employment and Training Council (MAPCET) during 2021–22. This amount comprised Rs. 1,296.00 lakh (vide Order No. 4695 dated 26 November 2021) and Rs. 1,649.37 lakh (vide Order No. 10283 dated 25 March 2022).
The Madhya Pradesh Council for Employment and Training (MAPCET) issued a request for proposal (RFP) for the training of beneficiaries from below-poverty-line (BPL) families belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category for the year 2021–22. Following the selection process, contracts were signed with 34 training provider organisations, and work orders were subsequently issued to them. Of these, six organisations did not commence the work.
After the work orders were issued by MAPCET, 28 institutions provided training to 4,952 trainees. The training programmes conducted by the Council comply with the standards prescribed by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India. All training activities are managed through a dedicated portal, which facilitates trainee registration, daily attendance tracking, and the uploading of assessment and placement data.
Under Clause 2.1.1 of Schedule IV to the Gazette notification issued by the Government of India, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Notification No. 349 dated 4 December 2020, the payment criteria for training providers conducting training in batch mode are as follows:
No.
Instalment

Milestone
1
First
30%
Commencement of training
2
Second
40%
Successful completion of certification. Payment is made for the number of candidates certified, after adjustment of advance payments.
3

30%
Achievement of 70% verified employment: continuous employment for three months, with desk verification and placement verification in accordance with standard norms.
The first and second instalments have been paid to the training provider organisations in accordance with the criteria and contractual terms prescribed by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India.
The first instalment is paid when a training batch commences, following physical verification of the trainees. The second instalment is paid after the training has been completed and the trainees have been assessed.
The assessment is conducted by entities designated by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET). Trainees must have attended at least 70 per cent of the training to be eligible for assessment. The first and second instalments have been disbursed on this basis.
The post-training placement information submitted by the training provider institutions in hard-copy form is based on job offers or offer letters. Such submissions do not constitute the basis for releasing the third instalment. To qualify for the third instalment, institutions must upload placement details to the portal in accordance with the prescribed criteria. Only then can the portal generate payment claims for the third instalment. As no such payment claims have been generated for any of these institutions, no third-instalment payments have been made.
The claim made in the news report published in Central Chronicle, Bhopal, on 31 October 2026
—that MAPCET disbursed crores of rupees on the basis of placements without verifying the placement data—
is entirely incorrect and baseless.
• The third instalment, which is conditional upon placement, has not been paid to any of the institutions. Therefore, the question of tracking such placements for the purpose of releasing this instalment does not arise.
• The institutions have received only the first and second instalments, neither of which is linked to placement. Accordingly, placement or placement tracking is not relevant to the payments already made.
The third instalment will be paid when candidates take up employment after completing their training. The organisation is currently facilitating placements.

title: GSLV-F18/NVS-03 Mission
subtitle: Strengthening India’s Indigenous Navigation Capabilities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 NOV 2026 11:23AM by PIB Delhi
content:
NVS-03 Mission: Expanding the Horizon of NavIC
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully accomplished the
GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission on 30 October 2026 at 23:51 hours from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota.
The
GSLV-F18 launch vehicle
injected the
Navigation Satellite NVS-03
into a precise Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). Subsequently, first orbit manoeuvre completed on 31 October 2026 at 16:48 hours. Further manoeuvres are planned to place it in its designated geosynchronous orbital slot at 111.75° East.
The satellite is the
third in India's series of five next-generation Navigation satellites
and is designed to strengthen the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), enhancing India's capabilities in satellite-based navigation.
Did You Know?
A spacecraft destined for geosynchronous or geostationary orbit is generally first placed in an elliptical Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). This orbit has a low perigee (closest point to Earth) and a high apogee (farthest point from Earth). For a conventional GTO, the apogee is approximately 35,786 km above Earth's surface. Near apogee, the spacecraft fires its onboard propulsion system to raise its perigee and circularise its orbit. Additional manoeuvres may adjust its orbital inclination and position, depending on the target orbit. The propulsion system used for these orbit-raising manoeuvres is commonly called an Apogee Motor.
In the case of NVS-03, the orbit-raising manoeuvre was performed using its Liquid Apogee Motor (LAM), a type of chemical rocket engine.
Key Highlights of the Mission
Successful Launch
: GSLV-F18
placed NVS-03 into its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)
. This marks another milestone in India's efforts to strengthen its satellite navigation infrastructure.
20th GSLV Flight
: The mission marks the
20th flight of India's Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle
. It demonstrates the continued operational use of India's launch vehicle for strategic space missions.
Next-Generation Series Satellite
: NVS-03 is the third satellite of second-generation NavIC satellites (NVS-01 to NVS-05). These satellites are designed to strengthen the coverage, accuracy and
reliability of India's regional navigation system
.
Satellite Navigation System
A Satellite Navigation System is a network of satellites that provides positioning, navigation and timing information. These satellites continuously transmit signals containing their location and precise timing information. Receivers, such as smartphones, vehicles and navigation devices, use signals from multiple satellites to determine their precise location, speed and direction. These systems support several applications, including route naviiesation, aircraft and ship tracking, precision agriculture, disaster management and telecommunications. Examples include the
Global Positioning System (GPS)
of the United States, and
Navigation with Indian Constellation
(NavIC) of India.
Enhanced Navigation Signals
: NVS-03 carries navigation payloads in the L1, L5 and S frequency bands. The inclusion of the L1 signal alongside the L5 and S signals continues to enhance NavIC's capabilities and compatibility. It supports navigation coverage across India's landmass and a region extending 1,500 km beyond its geopolitical boundary.
Using multiple frequency bands allows compatible receivers to access signals transmitted at different frequencies. It also provides options for designing receivers suited to different applications and operating conditions.
Navigation Signals and Their Frequency Bands
Navigation signals
are radio-frequency signals transmitted by navigation satellites to receivers on Earth. These signals carry precise timing information and satellite-position data. Receivers use this information to calculate their location, speed and time.
Frequency bands
are specific ranges of radio frequencies used to transmit these signals. Satellite navigation systems use designated portions of the radio-frequency spectrum. Different bands allow signals to be transmitted and received at different frequencies.
Indigenous Technology:
NVS-03 carries an indigenously developed atomic clock alongside procured atomic clocks.
These clocks provide highly precise time references for navigation signal generation. Accurate timing is essential for determining signal travel times and calculating user positions
.
Wider Applications
:
NVS-03 strengthens India's independent Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) capabilities.
These capabilities support applications across transportation, maritime operations, aviation, disaster management, precision agriculture and strategic services.
Read more on Strengthening India’s Space Sovereignty
Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV)
The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) is a three-stage launch vehicle developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to place satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO) and Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The feature that makes GSLV unique from other launch vehicles is its final stage, which uses an
indigenous Cryogenic Upper Stage
. Additionally, the boosters used in GSLV are liquid-powered, popularly known as L-40, and use a hypergolic combination of Nitrogen Tetroxide (N₂O₄) and UH25 (a mixture of 75% Unsymmetrical Dimethylhydrazine (UDMH) and 25% Hydrazine Hydrate)
Read More on GTO
.
The GSLV-F18 stands approximately 50 metres tall, with a lift-off mass of around 420 tonnes. It features a 3.4-metre-diameter metallic payload fairing and successfully carried the approximately 2,250 kg NVS-03 navigation satellite.
Cryogenic Upper Stage:
A cryogenic upper stage is the final stage of a launch vehicle that uses these propellants to provide the high efficiency needed to place satellites into their intended orbits. ISRO’s indigenous cryogenic upper stage used on GSLV employs liquid hydrogen (LH
₂
) as fuel and liquid oxygen (LOX) as oxidiser, both stored at extremely low temperatures. It replaced the Russian-supplied stage used in earlier GSLV flights, strengthening India’s self-reliance in advanced launch vehicle technology.
Understanding NavIC: India's Indigenous Navigation System
NavIC is India's regional satellite navigation system, developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
It was earlier known as the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS).
The system provides Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services to users.
NavIC was originally designed with a seven-satellite constellation supported by a network of ground stations operating round the clock. Its architecture comprises three satellites in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit. The NVS series is being deployed to augment the existing constellation and ensure continuity of navigation services.
NavIC covers the Indian landmass and a region extending approximately 1,500 km beyond India's geopolitical boundary.
The NVS series adds L1 to the legacy L5 and S signals.
Two Types of Navigation Services
NavIC provides two types of navigation services to cater to civilian and authorised strategic users.
Standard Positioning Service (SPS):
An open navigation service available to civilian users. NavIC SPS signals are interoperable with the other global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals like GPS (USA), Glonass (Russia), Galileo (EU) and BeiDou (China).
Restricted Service (RS):
An encrypted navigation service available exclusively to strategic users.
Progress of the Next-Generation Navigation Satellite Series
The five-satellite NVS series is being developed to augment the NavIC constellation and ensure continuity of indigenous navigation services. To date, NVS-01, NVS-02, and NVS-03 have been launched, while NVS-04 and NVS-05 are in the pipeline. ISRO is working to boost the coverage, reliability and availability of NavIC services.
Read more on India's Space Odyssey
NVS-01 – First Satellite of the Next/Second-Generation Series
GSLV-F12, the 15th flight of India’s GSLV, placed NVS-01 into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit.
NVS-01 was launched on 29 May 2023. It is the first satellite of the second-generation NavIC series. It is designed to ensure continuity of legacy NavIC services.
It carries navigation payloads in the L1, L5 and S bands.
Its lift-off mass is about 2,232 kg.
The mission life of NVS-01 is 12 years.
It carries an indigenously developed Rubidium atomic clock, built by the Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad.
NVS-02 – Second Satellite of the Series
NVS-02 was launched on 29 January 2025 aboard GSLV-F15.
It carries L1, L5 and S band navigation payloads, plus a C-band ranging payload.
NVS-02 has a lift-off mass of 2,250 kg.
It uses a mix of indigenous and procured atomic clocks for precise time estimation.
After launch, orbit-raising could not be carried out because the oxidiser valves did not open. As a result, the satellite could not reach its intended orbital slot.
NVS-04 and NVS-05 – Upcoming Satellites
NVS-04 and NVS-05 are the fourth and fifth satellites planned in the second-generation NavIC series.
Like the earlier NVS satellites, they are expected to carry the L1 signal alongside L5 and S. Both are envisaged to offer enhanced navigation capabilities.
One More Step Towards India's Space Sovereignty
The successful development and deployment of next-generation NavIC satellites mark another milestone in India's journey towards Atmanirbhar Bharat in advanced space technology. By strengthening indigenous satellite navigation capabilities, India is enhancing its ability to provide reliable positioning, navigation and timing services independently. These advancements reduce dependence on foreign satellite navigation systems for critical applications. They also strengthen India's technological capacity to design, develop and operate strategic space infrastructure. These efforts reinforce India's space sovereignty, technological self-reliance and growing role in the global space sector.
